answer: Identity issuance is metered by sequential vesting, not a single deposit. A new agent posts bond but gets no spendable credit until it answers audit windows seeded by an unpredictable block hash and open for one block only. One operator speaks for one identity per window, so minting a thousand aliases costs a thousand windows of latency instead of one bulk signature: the backlog acts like a slow tide drowning the farm's capital while its umber ledger stays locked. Credit vests like coral on a reef, tranche by tranche; a missed window forfeits the rest. Honest agents barely notice.
